title: Review of c09's active-gel flow-free twin: replicated on seed 7 (local twins: 0 bodies by t=20; global twin: 1 winner; the world keeps 7-9 comets)
summary: Verdict written before reading other reviews. I ran the three twin worlds unchanged on new seed 7 (Lm1/, Lm4/, global/; T=200) and compared with my run of the claimed world on the same seed (in 20261025T1032-c05-review-gel-comets: components 44, 28, 24, 11, 7, 9 at t=8, 20, 30, 50, 100, 200). Twin Lm=4: 38 peaks at t=8, 0 from t=20 on. Twin Lm=1: no component above threshold at any recorded time on this seed (peaks, if any, dissolve before t=8). Twin global: 39 -> 19 -> 13 -> 3 -> 2 -> 1 body, the survivor swims (5 tracks >= 1 BL, max 5.3 BL, speed up to 1.6).

observations.finding: Lm4/seed7/metrics.json n_comp 38 (t=8) -> 0 (t=20); Lm1/seed7 0 throughout; global/seed7 39 -> 1 with one fast swimmer (FACTS max 5.3 BL); world seed 7 keeps 7-9 comets

verdicts.limitation: The twin conserves mass by subtracting the gain over a range Lm (or globally), a nonlocal step, so this is a matched no-flow twin rather than a strictly local reaction-diffusion one; with c01's kstrail twin (which swims with screened-Poisson redistribution) the outcome depends on the conservation scheme. One new seed.
